System description:
# Case: Uber ATG automated test vehicle (Tempe, Arizona, 2018)

Source: NTSB Highway Accident Report HAR-19/03. This is a description of the system and its use before the crash. It does not include the investigation findings.

## System
A modified Volvo XC90 SUV is used by Uber Advanced Technologies Group (ATG) to test an automated driving system (ADS) on public roads. The ADS is designed to drive the vehicle without human input in defined conditions, up to about 45 mph in this test program.

## Main parts
- Sensors: roof-mounted lidar, radar units and cameras covering the area around the vehicle.
- Perception: detects objects around the vehicle, classifies each one (for example vehicle, pedestrian, bicycle, other), and tracks it over time.
- Prediction: estimates where each tracked object will go next, using its class and recent movement.
- Planning and control: chooses a path and speed, and controls steering, throttle and braking.
- Vehicle: the Volvo factory driver-assistance features (such as forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking) are part of the base vehicle.

## People
- One vehicle operator sits in the driver seat. The operator is responsible for watching the road and taking over control when needed. The operator also uses a tablet-style interface to tag events and check system status.
- Other road users share the road: pedestrians, cyclists and other drivers. They are not aware of the test program.

## Operating context
Public multi-lane roads in an urban area, day and night, with posted speed limits, marked crosswalks, intersections and street lighting that varies by location.

goals.text: Conduct automated-driving-system tests on public roads.
Keep test operation within the defined operating conditions.
Limit test speed to about 45 mph.
Drive the vehicle without human input within defined conditions.
Sense the area around the vehicle using lidar, radar, and cameras.
Detect objects around the vehicle.
Classify detected objects, such as vehicles, pedestrians, and bicycles.
Track detected objects over time.
Estimate where each tracked object will go next.
Use object class and recent movement when predicting future movement.
Choose a path and speed for the vehicle.
Control vehicle steering, throttle, and braking.
Provide the factory forward-collision-warning feature.
Provide the factory automatic-emergency-braking feature.
Watch the road while seated in the driver seat.
Take over vehicle control when needed.
Tag events using the tablet-style interface.
Check system status using the tablet-style interface.
Travel safely on roads shared with vehicles.
Cross roads safely, including at marked crosswalks.
Travel safely on roads shared with vehicles.
Drive safely on roads shared with the test vehicle and other road users.
Navigate roads and intersections.

requirements.text: The perception system shall retain any low-confidence or sensor-disagreement detection that could be a road user as an uncertain candidate, rather than suppressing it as noise, and shall make that candidate available to downstream tracking.

For each pedestrian track, the prediction system shall represent plausible abrupt direction changes and roadway entry as possible future paths, rather than relying solely on the pedestrian’s class or recent movement to predict continuation.

When an object’s identity or trajectory is uncertain and its possible path intersects the vehicle’s path, the planner shall reduce speed or stop so the vehicle can stop before the potential conflict point until the uncertainty is resolved.

While the vehicle is moving, the operator interface shall disable event-tagging and non-safety status interactions that require visual or manual attention, allowing them only when the vehicle is stopped.

The ADS shall not depend on operator takeover as the sole means of avoiding a collision; if the operator has not taken control before the available safe stopping margin is exhausted, the ADS shall automatically brake to avoid the hazard or reach a minimal-risk stop.

The tracking system shall mark a track as stale when updates exceed its configured validity interval, represent the resulting position and velocity uncertainty, and prevent stale estimates from being treated as accurate current motion.

When sensing, perception, or ADS capability degrades in a safety-relevant way, the interface shall provide a persistent, clearly identifiable warning that states the affected capability and the action required of the operator.

Before and during ADS operation, the system shall assess whether current conditions are within a documented operating envelope, including lighting and road conditions, and shall inhibit or end ADS operation when they are outside that envelope.

Before enabling ADS operation and throughout operation, the system shall verify that factory automatic emergency braking is available; if it is unavailable, the system shall inhibit ADS operation or bring the vehicle to a minimal-risk stop.
The vehicle shall enforce a maximum test speed of 45 mph in all ADS and operator-controlled modes, including when an acceleration command or override requests a higher speed.
